Evidence:
[1] The band were formed from the remnant members of a Scottish group called the Technicians who migrated to Australia in the 80s and who also attained top 40 status with their music releases, Hot for Love, Clockwork Clown and Sodier of Fortune through record companies Powderworks, EMI and BMG, and were published by MMA which was owned by legendary rock outfit INXS.
[2] Slik were a Scottish pop group of the mid-1970s, most notable for their UK no. 1 hit "Forever and Ever" in 1976.
[3] The New Scottish Group was a loose collection of artists based in Glasgow, who exhibited from 1942 to 1956.
[4] are a British new wave band, formed in London in 1973 as Tiger Lily.
